question.text: A close-ended Category III AIF's tenure can be extended by a maximum of how many years, and what is the required investor approval?

answer.text: Up to 3 years with 51% approval by value
Up to 2 years (with two 1-year extensions) requiring two-thirds approval by value
Up to 5 years with unanimous consent

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Regulation amended in 2023, close-ended Cat III AIFs can be extended for up to 2 years in two separate 1-year extensions, each requiring two-thirds approval of investors by value of investment. The Trap: Simple majority (51%) or unanimity is not the threshold; 5 years applies to LVFs only; indefinite extension is never allowed. Cross-Exam Context: Same 2-year extension rule applies to Cat I/II under XIX-A. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Start investor-extension outreach at least 90 days before original tenure expiry to ensure two-thirds consent is secured in time.
